scope: Independence and conditional-independence source block only; slides 3 through 11 inclusive.
selectionRationale: Slides 3 through 11 are the authoritative historical source for independence, conditional independence, the Toothache-Cavity-Catch example, common-cause examples, and the probability recap used across Meetings 9 and 10.
extractionPolicy: Every media part referenced by selected slides is copied byte-for-byte under its original PPTX filename. Full-slide renders exported by Microsoft PowerPoint at 1600 by 1200 preserve native text, equations, tables, DrawingML shapes, and animation final-state composition.

timingInventory.statement: Slides 3, 4, 7, and 10 contain native entrance/visibility build sequences. The exact timing XML and hashes are stored per slide. No selected slide contains a slide transition.

slideInventory.title: Conditional Independence
rawTextRuns: If I have a cavity, the probability that the probe catches in it doesn't depend on whether I have a toothache:
The same independence holds if I don
P(Toothache, Catch | Cavity) = P(Toothache | Cavity) P(Catch | Cavity)
One can be derived from the other easily
slideInventory.joinedTextForAudit: Conditional Independence | P(Toothache, Cavity, Catch) | If I have a cavity, the probability that the probe catches in it doesn't depend on whether I have a toothache: | P(+catch | +toothache, +cavity) = P(+catch | +cavity) | The same independence holds if I don | ’ | t have a cavity: | P(+catch | +toothache,  | - | cavity) = P(+catch|  | - | cavity) | Catch is  | conditionally independent |  of Toothache given Cavity: | P(Catch | Toothache, Cavity) = P(Catch | Cavity) | Equivalent statements: | P(Toothache | Catch , Cavity) = P(Toothache | Cavity) | P(Toothache, Catch | Cavity) = P(Toothache | Cavity) P(Catch | Cavity) | One can be derived from the other easily | 7

rawTextRuns: X, Y independent if and only if:
X and Y are conditionally independent given Z if and only if:
slideInventory.joinedTextForAudit: Probability Recap | Conditional probability | Product rule | Chain rule  | X, Y independent if and only if: | X and Y are conditionally independent given Z if and only if: | 11

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The equality P(X|Y)=P(X) is only defined for conditioning values with positive probability.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: State independence using P(X,Y)=P(X)P(Y), or qualify conditional equalities with P(Y)>0.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: A few displayed positive-event equalities can be read as sufficient evidence for variable-level conditional independence.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Conditional independence X independent of Y given Z requires the factorization or conditional equality to hold for every relevant value assignment with nonzero conditioning probability.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The compact Traffic-Umbrella-Raining and Fire-Smoke-Alarm graphics can be mistaken for empirical or causal proof.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Treat the graphical separation as a modeling assertion. Arrows and a common-cause pattern do not by themselves prove causation or conditional independence from observational data.

sourceCorrectionLedger.sourceIssue: The recap places universally valid probability identities beside independence-based factorizations without an explicit assumption boundary.
sourceCorrectionLedger.correction: Distinguish product and chain rules, which are probability identities where the conditionals are defined, from reduced factorizations that require an independence assumption.
